subject: Conditional Regional DR Coverage — Request for RTO/RPO Carve-In
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@econoserve.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@econoserve.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: multiregion failover coverage with tighter RTO/RPO

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, EconoServe needs a formal request so our security and operations teams can evaluate whether Redwood can commit to a stricter multiregion failover SLA for our production payment flows. Key asks: 

- Regional redundancy across two active regions (us-west and us-east) with automated failover.
- Target RTO: 15 minutes for switch-over; Target RPO: near-zero (sub-5s replication lag) for session/transaction state.
- Clear telemetry: per-failover timeline and post-incident artifacts (traces, timeline, activation time).
- Contractual carve-in/exception in the SOW rather than a temporary runbook.

I attached a spreadsheet with our operational requirements (EconoServe_DR_Requirements.xlsx). We have an internal deadline to present vendor options to our leadership by 2026-05-21. Can Redwood confirm feasibility and a proposed commercial structure for this level of coverage (including any standby fees, testing cadence, and liability carveouts)?

Appreciate a short reply with next steps.

Best,
Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Reliability, EconoServe
attachment: EconoServe_DR_Requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@econoserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multiregion failover coverage with tighter RTO/RPO

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. High-level response and proposed path forward below.

Short answer: we can support a conditional carve-in for tighter RTO/RPO, but it requires a combination of dedicated capacity, explicit replication configuration, and contractual limits that differ from our standard hosted SLA. Items to note: 

- Default hosted offering: warm-standby with typical failover RTO ~1h; RPO depends on workload and replication cadence.
- Option to meet your targets: Dedicated pool with pinned capacity across two regions + active replication (KV sync + prefix caching) and regular failover drills. This materially increases unit and standby cost.
- Contractual changes: we will require a scoped carve-in addendum that limits liability for pre-existing data loss windows and ties credits to measurable activation timelines.

Next steps I'd like to propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with Karthik/infra — schedule 60 minutes this week to review the attached requirements and map to replication/topology plans.
2) Commercial/Legal run: Marissa will lead the draft addendum and share a commercial proposal (standby fees + credit matrix).
3) Pilot: a 30-day POC to validate failover timelines and observability.

I attached an initial skeleton addendum for review (proposed_addendum_draft.docx). Marissa/Karthik — can you weigh in on feasibility and any gating constraints? Alex — can you share the internal decision criteria beyond leadership date?

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
attachment: proposed_addendum_draft.docx (document)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@econoserve.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-15T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multiregion failover coverage with tighter RTO/RPO

On Fri, May 14, 2026 at 10:03 AM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> I attached an initial skeleton addendum for review (proposed_addendum_draft.docx).

Alex / team — brief technical notes from infra: 

- Feasibility: Achievable, but only with Dedicated capacity pinned in both regions and synchronous-ish replication for critical tables/state. Our runtime supports cross-region KV replication but sub-5s RPO for all transactional state requires either active-active sharding or a small subset of state be replicated synchronously.
- Performance/latency tradeoffs: synchronous replication will increase write latency (we estimate ~20–60ms additional p99 depending on region hop). If that is unacceptable, we can scope the carve-in to a small set of critical keys (session tokens, in-flight transactions) to keep overall latency lower.
- Failover automation: we can automate activation via our routing policy; activation time depends on DNS/TCP timeouts + cache warming. With targeted engineering we can push activation to ~15 minutes consistently in tests.
- Operational obligations: we recommend a quarterly failover drill (with a defined runbook) and a telemetry contract where Redwood provides activation traces and KV sync metrics within X hours of an event.

I'll prepare an ops-level appendix showing topology options (active-active trimmed vs. active-passive with sync for critical keys). If you want, we can run a short synthetic test during the POC to measure end-to-end activation time.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@econoserve.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multiregion failover coverage with tighter RTO/RPO

Alex — looping in legal/commercial notes. Thanks for the clear asks.

Commercial considerations:
- Standby pricing: to guarantee pinned capacity in two regions we will propose a monthly standby fee (percent of committed throughput) plus consumption overage.
- Credits & caps: SLA credits will be provided for missed activation time, but we cannot accept uncapped liability for data loss. Proposed cap: monthly service fees x 3 for direct damages.
- Testing & acceptance: we need an acceptance test (30-day POC) with objective pass/fail criteria (activation time, RPO windows) before full contractual carve-in.
- Security/compliance evidence: we will provide runbook, activation logs and post-mortem artifacts, but cannot contractually commit to specific third-party audit outcomes.

I've attached a redline version of the addendum with commentary (redlines_ES_addendum.docx). A few contract items we will need the customer to accept: limited liability, defined maintenance windows for cross-region sync changes, and a documented escalation path for urgent mitigations.

If acceptable, I'll prepare a commercial term sheet for leadership review.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
attachment: redlines_ES_addendum.docx (document)

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@econoserve.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@econoserve.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: multiregion failover coverage with tighter RTO/RPO

Thanks Logan/Marissa/Karthik — this is helpful and aligned with our expectations. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) We agree to a 30-day POC with objective acceptance criteria. Please share the exact test plan and measurement points for activation time and RPO.
2) We will review liability cap language with legal, but can provisionally accept a capped approach if the credits and runbook evidence are robust.
3) For the technical scope, we prefer limiting synchronous replication to a narrowly-defined transaction set to avoid global write latency impacts. Karthik — please include a recommended key list in your ops appendix.

Could Redwood circulate an updated addendum with Marissa's redlines incorporated and a commercial term sheet by 2026-05-20? Our leadership meeting is 2026-05-21 EOD. If you can also include a proposed schedule for the POC (dates + required test accounts), that would be ideal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Reliability, EconoServe
